title: Clip a car air freshener onto a dashboard vent vane: fork over one pivoting vane, pushed home along it, vent aim kept
instruction: Clip the air freshener onto one of the centre vent's horizontal vanes, pushed all the way on, without changing where the vent is aimed.
context: Most drivers have clipped a vent air freshener onto a dashboard vent: every big brand (Febreze, Glade, Little Trees, Yankee Candle) sells this format, and many have tipped the vent doing it. The clip on its back is a two-prong fork whose 1.6 mm gap must straddle one 2 mm vane and be pushed straight on until the vane's front edge reaches the fork's root, where the springy prong grips it. The vanes are thin blades on pins held only by a light friction detent, so they stay wherever they are pushed: land the fork on a vane's face or push it on at an angle to the vane, and the vane tips (the air then blows at the roof or the floor); push it into the gap between two vanes and it has nothing to grip. Doing it right means lining the fork's 4.5 mm mouth up with one vane's edge to about a millimetre and pushing along that vane's plane, not just toward the vent.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (bases 610 apart at y = +305 and -305): x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. 1) Dashboard section, fixed to the table like a car's centre stack: dark grey moulded ABS (built: painted MDF round the printed ABS register), 600 wide (y -300 to +300), 150 deep, 190 tall, its vertical front face at x = 240. 2) Centre air vent in that face, built for real trials as the README's Building the vent says (a 3D-printed black ABS register with steel pins; no car vent publishes these sizes; they sit within the limits vent-mount makers publish for real louvres: blades under 3.5-4.2 thick, 10-34 deep, at least 8 between blades): opening 110 wide (y -175 to -65) and 70 tall (heights 95 to 165), a duct 45 deep behind it. Four horizontal vanes, black ABS, each 108 long, 17 deep and 2.0 thick, front edges flush with the face (x = 240), each on pins 8.5 behind its front edge at heights 107.5, 122.5, 137.5 and 152.5 (15 pitch, 13 clear between blades), turning +-30 degrees and held at any angle by a friction detent of 0.030 N m about the pins (0.025 N m once moving), set on the built vent with an O-ring and collar on each pin: 330 g hung from a vane's front edge leaves it level, 390 g turns it; all start level. Seven fixed vertical vanes start 26 behind the face, out of the fork's reach. 3) Air freshener: a Febreze CAR vent clip (2 mL scented oil when new), its clip already clicked open (activated); real trials use a used-up clip, its oil gone (README). Body a rounded rectangle 41 wide, 38 tall, 16 thick, 7 g. Fork out of the middle of its back, at right angles: two prongs 20 long, 7 wide, 1.4 thick at the root, 1.6 apart, each turned out over its last 3 to a 4.5 mouth; the lower prong is fixed, the upper one sprung (1.0 N at rest, 1.5 N spread to 2.0 over a vane, opens at most 0.8 more). (Body, fork and spring figures are estimates, not measured on a bought clip; the maker publishes none, and the fork's lie inside its patent's ranges. The simulated spring is stiffer than a beam calculation of this fork (0.39-0.78 N; README). Before the first trial the bought clip is checked: gap 1.35-1.95, mouth 3.5-5.5, prongs 18-22, on a kitchen scale spreading force at most 150 g and push-on force at most 340 g, and the 100 g hold.) It stands on its flat bottom edge on a black rubber console mat (150 x 120 x 3, centre (165, -60)), its centre at (170, -60, 22), fork level and pointing at the dashboard (+x). The vent's centre on the face is at (240, -120, 130): the clip starts 298 and the third vane's front edge is 303 (horizontally) from the right arm's base. Frictions (estimates): ABS 0.40, the clip's polypropylene 0.50, rubber mat 0.80.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run (real trial: the end of the video, then a ruler, a protractor and a 100 g weight). Any of the four vanes counts. Engaged: the vane lies between the two prongs (real: seen from the side, the vane between both prongs) with at least 8 mm of the 20 mm prongs over it (the vane's front edge 12 mm or less from the fork's root). Home: the vane's front edge within 2 mm of the root. Let go: both grippers' tool points at least 3 cm from the clip and from the vent opening. Then, once it has been engaged, let go and still for 1 s (three points on the clip moved under 1 mm and no vane turned more than 1 degree over that second), a hold check: the clip is pulled straight down with 1 N for 2 s (real: a 100 g weight hung from a thread looped round the clip's body, lowered by hand without touching the clip); it must move less than 2 mm. Aim: the largest angle any vane is turned from level at the end (protractor; the vanes keep any angle they are pushed to). Square: the angle between the fork and the dashboard face's normal (real: a protractor against the clip's back face, from above and from the side). Score 0: not engaged (in a gap, on a vane's face, on a prong, dropped), still touched, hold check failed, or the aim off by more than 15 degrees (the vent knocked). Otherwise aim is ok up to 5 degrees and minor from 5 to 15; square is ok up to 15 degrees, minor from 15 to 30, major beyond. Home with aim and square ok: 1.0; home with one minor: 0.75; home with two minors: 0.5; engaged but not home (root gap 2-12 mm) with both ok: 0.5; not home with a minor: 0.25; square major (home or not): 0.25. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Pull the clip straight off its vane along the vane's plane, stand it on its flat bottom edge on its mark on the mat (within 1 cm), fork toward the dashboard, and set all four vanes level (within 1 degree). The same clip is reused; the vent is never removed. Zero object jitter.
fidelity: True-size rigid parts. Each vane has its own pins and detent; the rear link that turns a car's vanes together is left out, as in the built vent. The fork's sprung prong is a plate on a sprung slide, 1.5 N on a vane (beam calculation: 0.39-0.78 N), with a numerical armature; its barbs are left out. The oil is mass only. The clip starts clicked open, standing on its flat edge. The vent is built to the simulated sizes and detent; the clip's sizes, spring and mass and all frictions are estimates.
